rationale: The answer gets the central structure right. It separates transparency-policy disclosure from daily public holdings disclosure. It also correctly treats periodic public holdings as conditional on giving APs and market makers daily information sufficient for arbitrage, not as a blanket exemption, which matches the grader note. However, it leaves out several substantive requested facts. On the transparency policy, it names only the prospectus and website. It omits the KID/KIID and marketing materials and does not mention disclosing where portfolio or iNAV information is available. It also loosely recasts the policy as being about AP/market-maker information. On the periodic route, it omits the CBI Q&A 1012 conditions: arbitrage information provided on a nondiscriminatory basis, prospectus disclosure of that information, procedures for impaired arbitrage and investor information requests, and public quarter-end holdings within 30 business days. It does not say that daily holdings disclosure is also nondiscriminatory or identifies positions and quantities. It also omits the iNAV calculation and frequency disclosure. The core mechanism is correct but lacks material conditions.
